critical_findings.finding: Markdown rendering or link handling could permit client-side script execution (XSS) in the generated static site (e.g., raw HTML passthrough, unsafe URL schemes like javascript:), compromising readers.

closure.closure_target: Prevent script execution from note content by default: disable raw HTML (or sanitize), block unsafe URL schemes, set safe link attributes, and add an automated XSS regression suite tied to build/test.

critical_findings.finding: Ingestion could unintentionally read/include files outside the intended notes root (symlink following, path traversal, glob mistakes), leaking local secrets into the published static site.

closure.closure_target: Constrain discovery to a declared root; default to not following symlinks; enforce .md-only allowlist; reject any resolved paths escaping root; generate an inclusion manifest for review.

critical_findings.finding: Slug/URL collisions (case-insensitive filesystems, same filename in different folders, inconsistent normalization) can overwrite pages and cause forward links/backlinks to resolve unpredictably or incorrectly.

closure.closure_target: Define and implement a canonical slug strategy (path-based + normalization rules); detect collisions during build and fail with actionable errors; ensure link resolution uses the same canonicalization as URL generation.

critical_findings.finding: Core features (especially search index loading) may fail when opening pages via file:// or when deployed under a subpath (e.g., GitHub Pages), due to fetch/XHR restrictions and/or incorrect basePath-relative asset URLs.

closure.closure_target: Add configurable basePath and test non-root deployments; for local preview, either (a) avoid runtime fetch for the index (bundle/inline) or (b) detect file:// and present instructions to run a local static server; add regression tests for both modes.
closure.earliest_prevention_stage: M4 (Client-Side Search) for file:// search behavior; M1/M2 for basePath-safe link/asset generation

critical_findings.finding: Link canonicalization mismatches (anchors, URL-encoding, relative path resolution) can produce partial or incorrect backlink sets even when forward links appear to work, undermining R21 correctness.

closure.closure_target: Implement a single canonical internal link model used by both URL/slug generation and link parsing; normalize/resolve relative paths; standardize handling of anchors (strip for page identity); add fixtures for encoded characters, anchors, and relative paths.

critical_findings.finding: Client-side search index generation and runtime querying may become too large/slow at scale, causing long build times, large JS/JSON payloads, slow queries, or browser crashes; this risks failing R19/SM7 in realistic corpora.

closure.closure_target: Define expected scale targets (Q3), adopt index-size controls (tokenization/stop-words/compression) and possibly lazy-loading/sharding; add CI performance budgets and benchmark fixtures; document hard limits/exclude options.
closure.earliest_prevention_stage: M4 (Client-Side Search), with Q3 answered before committing performance-sensitive implementation

critical_findings.finding: Generated output or search index/logging could inadvertently disclose sensitive information such as absolute filesystem paths, excluded/private note names, or other local environment details, creating privacy risk for published sites.

closure.closure_target: Ensure build artifacts never contain absolute source paths (use relative IDs only); support exclude globs and a private flag; generate an inclusion manifest; scrub logs intended for publication.

critical_findings.finding: Watch mode/incremental rebuild (if implemented) can produce stale backlinks, tags, or search index after edits/renames/deletes, leading to confusing inconsistencies that are hard to diagnose.

closure.closure_target: If watch mode is shipped, maintain a dependency graph to trigger recomputation of affected pages plus global artifacts (backlinks/search); add edit/rename/delete tests; provide a reliable full-rebuild fallback.

critical_findings.finding: The system may be vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) if raw HTML is enabled or unsafe URL schemes (e.g., 'javascript:') are not blocked during Markdown rendering. A user with commit access to the notes could inject scripts that execute in the browsers of site readers, compromising security.

critical_findings.finding: The file ingestion process could be vulnerable to path traversal if input paths are not sanitized, or if symbolic links are followed outside the specified root directory. This could allow a malicious commit to include sensitive local files from the build environment into the public static site.

closure.evidence: { "artifact_ref": "risk_gov_canonical_v1", "entity_id": "K9", "json_pointer": "/risk_register/8", "quote": "Path traversal or unintended file inclusion during ingestion..." }
closure.closure_target: Implementation and testing of input path sanitization within the file ingestion component (C2), ensuring the build process cannot read outside the specified input directory. Validate during M1.

critical_findings.finding: Without a strict, specified standard for internal link syntax (e.g., standard Markdown vs. [[wikilinks]]), the system may fail to correctly parse links, resulting in broken navigation and incomplete or incorrect backlink lists. This undermines a core feature of the system and is dependent on resolving blocking question Q1.

closure.evidence: { "artifact_ref": "risk_gov_canonical_v1", "entity_id": "K1", "json_pointer": "/risk_register/0", "quote": "Link/backlink resolution errors due to ambiguous or mixed internal link syntax..." }
closure.closure_target: Formal resolution of open question Q1 to define a canonical link syntax. This decision must be documented before M1 begins, and the syntax must be implemented and tested during M2.

critical_findings.finding: Without a clear specification for how tags are represented (e.g., YAML frontmatter vs inline #tags), the system can misinterpret or miss tags entirely, leading to incorrect tag pages and broken tag-based navigation. This is dependent on resolving blocking question Q2.

closure.evidence: { "artifact_ref": "risk_gov_canonical_v1", "entity_id": "K2", "json_pointer": "/risk_register/1", "quote": "Tag extraction inconsistency due to unspecified or mixed tag formats..." }
closure.closure_target: Formal resolution of open question Q2 to define a canonical tag format. This decision must be documented before M1 begins, and the format must be implemented and tested during M3.

critical_findings.finding: The build process may be non-deterministic due to factors like unstable file ordering or locale-dependent sorting. This results in inconsistent site output for the same source notes, creating noisy diffs in version control and undermining reproducibility and caching.

closure.evidence: { "artifact_ref": "risk_gov_canonical_v1", "entity_id": "K6", "json_pointer": "/risk_register/5", "quote": "Non-deterministic builds...produce noisy diffs and inconsistent site output..." }
closure.closure_target: Implement stable sorting for all collections (notes, tags, etc.) and pin all dependencies with a lockfile. A reproducibility test should be added to CI to validate a second clean build produces identical output.

critical_findings.finding: As the number of notes grows, the client-side search index asset can become excessively large, increasing the site's initial load time and memory consumption. In-browser query performance may also degrade, leading to a poor user experience on large note collections.

closure.evidence: { "artifact_ref": "risk_gov_canonical_v1", "entity_id": "K4", "json_pointer": "/risk_register/3", "quote": "Client-side search index size/quality/performance may degrade at scale..." }
closure.closure_target: Define performance targets based on expected scale (Q3). Implement and benchmark the search solution in M4 (DL18) against a representative dataset to validate index size, load time, and query latency.

critical_findings.finding: If watch mode is implemented, failure to correctly track dependencies can lead to stale content after file edits, renames, or deletions. For example, renaming a note title might not update its backlinks, or deleting a note might not remove it from the search index, leading to data inconsistency.

closure.evidence: { "artifact_ref": "risk_gov_canonical_v1", "entity_id": "K14", "json_pointer": "/risk_register/13", "quote": "Incorrect incremental rebuild/watch behavior...can lead to stale search index/backlinks..." }
closure.closure_target: If watch mode is implemented (M5), it must include a test suite for file edits, renames, and deletions, verifying that all dependent artifacts (backlinks, tag pages, search index) are correctly updated.
